- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if price is trending sharply upward, forecast should be capped at 1–2 std dev above recent mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average smoothing for 30d forecasts.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often fails to recognize it; apply a “lag correction” — reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 1–3% to align with observed drop.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.9) correlate with model overconfidence; if sentiment >0.8 for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–6% to reflect diminishing momentum.
